propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation fallback (file-level git blame over impacted paths) produces no provenance marker distinguishing derived edges from explicitly supplied ones, making confidence uncomputable

On a population of 88 closed bugs carrying caused_by edges, the real derive_caused_by mechanism agrees with recorded edges 43%, disagrees 7%, and abstains 50% (mostly due to no-majority or unresolvable culprit)
Against 8 bugs with independently proven origins, the deriver reproduced 0 correct attributions, abstained on 7, and named the innocent party (wrong-target) on 1 confident output
The dominant defect shapes in this codebase (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions) are structurally hard for file-level blame and correlate with deriver abstentions and misattribution

History drift (renamed/moved files, dissolved majorities, unresolving commits) accounts for 44 of 44 abstentions but does not explain the single wrong-target case, which is a defect-shape problem inherent to blame

A blame-derived edge must become distinguishable from an explicitly supplied edge via a provenance marker on the link event, so consumers can weight or exclude guesses from metrics like escape-rate lenses
